description:
Generic dense and sparse linear algebra over arbitrary finite fields, built on `FieldVec<F: FiniteField>` from the GF(p^n) epic (e095a100). Competes with Magma/Sage on ergonomics and with fflas-ffpack on throughput.

## Primary goals

1. **UX ergonomics**: Armadillo-style API — operator overloads (`*`, `+`, `-`, scalar), `.t()`, `submat`, free functions (`solve`, `inv`, `det`, `rank`), Display pretty-printing, expression-template proxy types so `&a * &b + &c` fuses into one `fgemm`. API parity with `BitMatrix` via a shared `MatrixLike<Elem>` trait. See `dev/plans/armadillo_ux_mapping.md`.
2. **Performance**: delayed-reduction kernels (bounds via `FiniteField::Wide`), SIMD dispatch, blocked + Strassen-Winograd matmul, block-recursive factorizations reducing everything to `gemm`. See `dev/plans/fflas_ffpack_analysis.md` + `dev/plans/dumas_pernet_takeaways.md`.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] **Dense `FieldMatrix<F>`** with the full BitMatrix-parity public surface and Armadillo-shape free functions, shared `MatrixLike<Elem>` trait implemented by both `BitMatrix` and `FieldMatrix<F>`. No behavior change to existing `BitMatrix` users.
- [hard] **Expression-template algebra** designed and implemented — canonical fusions (`A·B + βC`, `αA + βB`, `Aᵀ·B`) collapse to a single kernel call.
- [hard] **Matrix multiplication** with delayed reduction (Dumas–Pernet §1.2) and Strassen–Winograd (§1.4) with correct bound propagation (theorem 4). All four owned/ref operator combos supported.
- [hard] **PLE decomposition** (§2.2, algorithm 2.5) with block-recursion reducing to `gemm` + `trsm`. Handles non-generic rank profile correctly. LU / row-echelon / RRE / rank / nullspace are projections of PLE.
- [hard] **Triangular primitives** `trsm / trmm / trtri / trtrm` as first-class, block-recursive kernels (§2.1, algorithms 2.1–2.4).
- [hard] **Matrix inversion, solve, determinant** built on PLE + triangular primitives. No bespoke LU.
- [hard] **Characteristic & minimal polynomial** (§3) — deterministic cubic baseline + sub-cubic Las-Vegas variant where the field permits.
- [hard] **Sparse `FieldMatrix`** with CSR/CSC representations, SpMV/SpMM, naming parity with `SpBitMatrix`.
- [hard] **Benchmarking** — per-story criterion micro-benchmarks at every implementation story; terminal benchmark story (64c88ae4) produces a published run against `fflas-ffpack` (GF(p), GF(2^m)) and `M4RI` (GF(2)) from a pinned container image.
- [hard] **Correctness on rank-deficient inputs** — PLE and derivatives (inv returning None, rank, nullspace) tested on explicitly rank-deficient matrices.
- [hard] All public items documented with `# Examples` doctests, `# Complexity`, `# Panics` where applicable.
- [hard] All `cargo-ci`, `code-review`, `doc-review` gates pass on every child story.
- [aspirational] GF(p): within 2× of `fflas-ffpack` on matmul / PLE / solve at n = 1024.
- [aspirational] GF(2^m): exceed `fflas-ffpack` on matmul at n ≥ 256 (direct PCLMULQDQ vs. float-BLAS).
- [aspirational] GF(2): within 1.5× of `M4RI` on matmul at n = 1024.

## Architecture

- Lives in `crates/gf2-core/src/field/matrix.rs` (dense), `field/sparse_matrix.rs` (sparse), plus `matrix_like.rs` (shared trait).
- `BitMatrix` remains the specialized GF(2) path; gains only a trivial `MatrixLike<bool>` impl. No behavior change.
- Matrix multiply dispatches to `FieldVec::dot_product` as the inner kernel; SIMD and delayed reduction happen in the vec layer.
- Block-recursive factorizations (PLE, echelon, inv, solve, charpoly) reduce to `gemm` + `trsm/trmm/trtri/trtrm` — paper's central thesis.
- Expression-template proxy layer fuses `A·B + βC` and friends into one `gemm` call.

## Non-goals

- Eigenvalue decomposition (not meaningful over finite fields).
- Floating-point BLAS integration — we use direct SIMD kernels.
- Replacing `BitMatrix` for GF(2).
- Blackbox iterative methods (Wiedemann, Lanczos) — Dumas–Pernet §4, deferred.
- Sparse matrix reordering (Markowitz, minimum-degree) — §5, deferred.
- RNS for large primes — research task `0a7e2555` already DONE; revisit when needed.
- Bitslicing for F₃, F₅, F₇ — §1.1; no current downstream consumer.

## References

## Scope Amendment — SOTA closure moved to `97bf0879`

The FieldMatrix implementation epic closes on API completeness, correctness, documentation, and a truthful baseline/post-PPC benchmark publication. It does **not** require final state-of-the-art parity against external systems.

The benchmarking success criterion is now interpreted as: `64c88ae4` publishes a reproducible baseline/post-PPC scorecard that identifies performance gaps and links the raw evidence. The new epic `97bf0879` ("Close gf2-core SOTA performance gaps") owns the work needed to close those gaps to the 1.5x SOTA threshold.

The three aspirational performance bullets in this epic are therefore checkpoint goals for `b117c95e` and `97bf0879`, not blockers for closing `bb85c68a` once its implementation and baseline publication children pass their gates.
title: Implement generic finite field linear algebra (FieldMatrix)
